compatibility_notes: Two ports match only when every field the target requires is satisfied. Missing required information returns UNKNOWN. Every conversion or inference must be declared and versioned.
description: One molecular structure represented as a SMILES string, with the optional SMILES syntax features that the producing port may emit and the receiving port can interpret without discarding their meaning.

examples.conditions: Both ports make the same complete declarations for this profile.
examples.title: Identical molecular SMILES contracts are exact matches
examples.why: Both ports declare the same molecular SMILES format and syntax features.

examples.conditions: The source feature set is a subset of the target feature set.
examples.title: An input may accept more syntax features than the output emits
examples.why: Every optional syntax feature the output may emit is understood by the input.

examples.conditions: One port omits the required syntax feature declaration.
examples.title: Missing syntax capability information is unknown
examples.why: The comparison cannot determine which optional SMILES features the output may emit.

examples.conditions: The output may emit stereochemistry and the input does not declare support for it.
examples.title: Unsupported stereochemistry is incompatible
examples.why: Passing the string could discard stereochemical meaning that the output may encode.

examples.conditions: The output may emit isotopes and the input does not declare support for them.
examples.title: Unsupported isotopes are incompatible
examples.why: Passing the string could discard isotope information that the output may encode.

examples.conditions: The output may emit disconnected components and the input does not declare support for them.
examples.title: Unsupported disconnected components are incompatible
examples.why: The input cannot safely consume salts or other dot-disconnected components the output may emit.

examples.conditions: The required molecular SMILES declarations match and only excluded canonicalisation metadata differs.
examples.title: Canonicalisation labels do not gate this profile
examples.why: This connection consumes molecular SMILES and does not require a particular canonical form.

intended_use: Connecting a model output that emits one validated molecular SMILES string to a model input that accepts the declared SMILES syntax features. The first pilot connection is a REINVENT 4 sampling output passed to a Chemprop 2.3.1 molecular input wrapper.
label: Molecular SMILES
limitations: This profile checks interface compatibility, not whether a SMILES string is chemically correct or denotes the intended molecule.
A producing wrapper must parse and validate each emitted string before claiming this profile; a declaration alone does not validate runtime values.
It does not treat different SMILES strings as the same molecule or standardise tautomers, protonation, salts, charge, aromaticity or atom order.
It does not cover reaction SMILES, CXSMILES, files, tables or batches of molecules.
Canonical and non-canonical SMILES are both in scope because canonicalisation is not required for this connection.
name: molecular-smiles
scientific_claim: This profile checks whether two model interfaces fit together. It does not show that a model is scientifically valid or clinically safe.
